sampleArticle.title: We're Up and Running
sampleArticle.lead: We’ve long wanted to bring together in one place everything that Plus In Plus has become: our approach, our services, and the projects through which we put ideas to the test. Now our new website is live—and it’s more than just an updated showcase. It’s a clearer story of how we help products become cohesive and ready for growth.
sampleArticle.closing: The new Plus In Plus website is now live. Welcome.

sections.title: It's Not Just About Design
paragraphs: Plus In Plus began with a desire to make ideas clear and expressive. Over time, it became clear that a visual solution alone wasn’t enough. For a product to work, you need to tie together its goals, user experience, interface, and technological foundation.

That’s why today we take a broader view of the task—from the initial questions about the product to design, design systems, and front-end development. We care not only about how a single screen looks, but also about how all parts of the product work together.

sections.title: Why We Needed a New Website
sections.subtitle: The website was meant to answer a simple question: how can Plus In Plus be useful to your team?
paragraphs: We restructured the site to immediately highlight our main areas of focus: web design and UX, design systems, and front-end development. We also highlighted our systematic approach—where a solution helps not only launch a product but also develop it further.

The visual language also became part of this narrative: clean typography, white space, and precise details create a sense of clarity rather than clutter. And snippets of interfaces and projects allow visitors to see our approach in context.

sections.title: Experience That Grows Alongside Our Products
paragraphs: An important part of our work consists of our own projects and ecosystems: Ozone and Plus For Play. They help us view a product not just through a single mockup, but through real-world scenarios, user feedback, and iterative development.
This experience shapes how we approach new challenges: first, we understand the context; then, we build a clear system of solutions; and only then do we move on to implementation.

sections.title: What's Next
paragraphs: Launching a website isn’t the end—it’s the beginning of the next phase. We’ll be adding case studies, articles on design and development, and new insights from our product practice.
If you have an idea that needs to be turned into a clear and scalable product—tell us about it. Let’s discuss the best place to start.

directions.heading: A design practice and our own product

product.title: Line Launcher
product.description: A Minecraft launcher for game projects: one provider, one launcher, a build branded for the client.

lineLauncher.title: Line Launcher
lineLauncher.lead: A minimal Minecraft launcher for game projects. One provider, one launcher: the player signs in and presses Play instead of picking servers and typing addresses.
lineLauncher.releaseNote: There are no public releases yet: the build lives in the open repository. Installers will appear here only after the project owner publishes them.

download.title: Download
download.unavailable: No public builds yet — files appear after the first release

whatsNew.title: What's new
whatsNew.note: A short read of the Line Launcher release history.

lineLauncher.whatLead: The launcher knows its project address: it is baked in at build time. The player never chooses a provider or types a server address — a single sign-in opens the project catalogue.
lineLauncher.whatBody: The project owner assembles the app for their own brand: name, logo, icons and API address. The player gets a launcher that contains nothing but that project.

features.title: First run
features.text: A short intro, then the choice of language, background gradient and motion — before signing in.

features.title: One sign-in
features.text: A project account, not a Microsoft one. Servers with online-mode=true still require separate server-side authorisation.

features.title: Server catalogue
features.text: Last choice, search, filters and live status when the provider publishes it.

features.title: Project build
features.text: Play, verify integrity, prepare a build in advance or roll a release back.

features.title: Minecraft mode
features.text: A provider-supported build and one-click launch.

features.title: Settings
features.text: Memory, Java, appearance, window and data.

features.title: Wardrobe and profile
features.text: A skin history with previews and a profile with a 3D skin view.

features.title: Player guidebook
features.text: Six chapters of a built-in guide with GIF demos and a static poster under reduced motion.

lineLauncher.privacyBody: Telemetry is optional and off by default: consent is given separately and sits next to the provider policy link.
lineLauncher.buildBody: The build is branded for the project: name, logo, icons and API address. One provider, one launcher, no extra screens.

work.title: Studio work
work.lead: Our own product, brand and website — everything you can check right now. Client projects are published only with the client's permission.

studio.title: Plus In Plus design practice
studio.lead: We design visual systems for brands: identity, signage and wayfinding, digital layouts and event collateral. We start from meaning — position and structure first, form second. In parallel we build our own product, Line Launcher.

facts.label: Language
facts.value: One primitive: grain and soft light

studio.processLead: Four steps with no setup wizards: you always know where the project stands and what is needed from you.

process.title: Brief
process.body: We unpack the task: where the work will be seen, what has to change, and what limits exist on timing and production.

process.title: Concept
process.body: We show two or three directions with reasoning — what works for your case and why.

process.title: Artwork
process.body: We build the final layout: typography, colour, surfaces, print and installation requirements.

process.title: Handover
process.body: We hand over source files and stay for production: checking files, colours and how the artwork lands on site.
